**r01 — Redis / user-entry TTL**
**Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this repo** (a case-insensitive grep for `redis` across all Go/TS/mod files returns zero hits; no client dependency in `go.mod`). The cache layer is a **process-local in-memory cache**: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:66`, backed by `sync.Map`, TTL expiry + a background cleanup goroutine, `Close` at `:187`). Three instances are created in `store.New`: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (`store/store.go:47-52`). There is **no user-specific TTL** — all three share one `cache.Config` with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:40-45`; identical defaults in `cache.DefaultConfig()` at `store/cache/cache.go:57-63`). User entries are written by `Store.CreateUser`/`UpdateUser`/`ListUsers`/`GetUser` (`store/user.go:91,132,142,152,166`) and invalidated on delete (`store/user_delete.go:40`). Nothing calls `SetWithTTL` with a custom value for users.

**r02 — per-user API rate-limiting middleware**
**Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase.** Greps for `RateLimit`, `ratelimit`, and `rate.limit` produce no implementation — the only hit is an aspirational comment about email sending (`internal/email/doc.go:86`). The Echo middleware stack is only `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:50-51`), and the Connect interceptor chain is Metadata / Logging / Recovery / Auth (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:22,98,165,208`). The closest things to throttling are concurrency semaphores, not request-rate limits: `thumbnailSemaphore` (3) and `imageProcessingSemaphore` (2) in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60-61`, `maxConcurrentThumbnails` in `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:116`, and a `maxAPIRequestBytes` body cap (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`).

**r03 — nightly database-cleanup job time**
**Premise is wrong: no such job exists and no cron scheduler is running.** `internal/scheduler` is a self-contained, currently **unused** library — the only files importing it are its own tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`); no production code calls `scheduler.New`, `Register`, or `Start` (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:54,70,91`). The `"0 2 * * *" // 2 AM daily` "daily-cleanup" you may have seen is an illustrative snippet in the **package doc comment** (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:16-18`), not a registered job. The only real background work is the s3presign runner on a 12-hour `time.Ticker` (see h01), started in `server/server.go:158-172`.

**r04 — NATS vs RabbitMQ for webhook workers**
**Premise is wrong on both counts: there is no message broker.** Greps for `nats`, `NATS`, `rabbit`, and `amqp` return zero hits repo-wide, and `go.mod` has no broker client. The actual mechanism is an **in-process buffered Go channel**: `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by **4 goroutines** started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the event with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`); each worker calls `webhook.Post` (`:120`) to do the HTTP POST. The queue is therefore neither durable nor shared across processes — pending webhooks are lost on restart.

**r05 — GraphQL schema location**
**Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL in this project** — no `.graphql`/`.gql` files, no `gqlgen`/`graphql-go` dependency, and zero case-insensitive matches for `graphql` in Go or TS sources. The public API is **Protobuf-defined RPC**: service definitions live in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`), generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/`. They are served two ways from `APIV1Service.RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:64`): **Connect RPC** handlers (`server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go`, `connect_services.go`) and a **gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON** mapping (`proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`). Alongside that sit plain Echo HTTP surfaces — the file server (`/file/...`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), SSE (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), `/healthz` (`server/server.go:64`), and an MCP endpoint (`server/router/mcp/service.go`, registered at `server/server.go:97`).
